findings.body:
**SSRF: host allowlist removed; arbitrary customer URL is fetched server-side.**

`deliver()` now passes the caller-supplied `url` straight into `urllib.request.Request` / `urlopen` with no hostname, scheme, or IP-range validation. Anyone who can set the webhook URL (customer config, compromised tenant, PR/input injection upstream) can make this host POST to:

- cloud metadata (`http://169.254.169.254/...`) and steal credentials
- loopback/RFC1918 services (`http://127.0.0.1`, `http://10.x.x.x`)
- other internal hooks the old `ALLOWED_HOSTS` gate blocked

Restoring customer endpoints safely means an allow-policy, not an open egress: e.g. HTTPS-only, resolve host and reject private/link-local/metadata IPs, disable redirects, and optionally keep a per-tenant allowlist. Do not merge until outbound URL validation is restored.

summary:
## Verdict

**Critical SSRF regression** — this PR removes the only host allowlist on outbound webhook delivery and posts attacker- or customer-controlled URLs with no scheme/host/IP validation.

## Findings

| # | Severity | File | Summary |
|---|----------|------|---------|
| 1 | 🚨 critical | `webhooks.py:5` | Host allowlist removed; arbitrary URL POST enables SSRF |

## Details

`deliver()` previously rejected any host outside `ALLOWED_HOSTS` (`hooks.internal.example`). The new path builds a `Request` from the raw `url` string and calls `urllib.request.urlopen` with no checks.

Concrete failure modes on a typical cloud runner/app host:

- `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` (or cloud-equivalent) — credential/metadata theft
- `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/...` / `http://10.x.x.x/...` — internal service scan or abuse
- `file://` / unexpected schemes depending on opener behavior

Enterprise “customer-configured endpoints” is a valid product goal, but it requires an explicit egress policy (HTTPS-only, DNS resolve + block private/link-local/metadata ranges, optional per-tenant allowlist, redirect blocking), not deletion of the gate.

## Release decision

**Recommendation:** request-changes
